ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory determination and ongoing monitoring of Politically Exposed Persons, their family members, and close associates in accordance with FINTRAC guidance under the PCMLTFA; mandatory screening against United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 20; OFAC SDN screening is additionally required where payment rails or US-based processors such as Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal are used; all adverse hits must be escalated to the compliance officer and reported to FINTRAC where reasonable grounds exist.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ServiceOntario ONBIS (Ontario Business Information System), administered by the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal corporate name must be capable of being set out in letters of the Roman alphabet. English and French forms are acceptable in Ontario. A non-Latin script trade name requires a Roman-alphabet transliteration for the mandatory NUANS search and official records. The name must include 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', or an authorized abbreviation such as Ltd., Inc., or Corp., and must not be identical to or confusable with an existing Ontario or federally registered corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words or expressions creating the impression of government sponsorship, public office, or regulated professional status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant must review the written rejection grounds from the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, prepare an administrative review request addressed to the Director, setting out distinguishability arguments and any supplementary NUANS search evidence. The request should be submitted through ONBIS or by registered mail before the expiry of any current reservation. The Director's decision may be challenged by judicial review to the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. J.1, and proceedings must generally be commenced within 30 days of written notification. An approved name reservation may be renewed for an additional 90-day period before expiry if the articles have not yet been filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the service provider supplies a real physical street address in Ontario and is capable of accepting service of process. A post-office box or mail-forwarding-only address is not acceptable. For ISIC 3240 handmade resin dice casting, the registered office may be virtual, but the actual production, inventory, and occupational health and safety premises must be independently established at a separate commercial address satisfying municipal zoning, fire safety, and environmental requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Routine physical inspection risk at incorporation is estimated at 2%-5%; the likelihood increases to an estimated 10%-20% once HST/GST registration, commercial leasing, import of resin materials, or workplace safety obligations trigger CRA or municipal by-law verification. Unannounced on-site inspections by CRA or municipal authorities are possible but not standard at the pre-incorporation stage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, as amended (OBCA); applicable sections include s. 4 (incorporation), s. 5 (articles), s. 6 (certificate of incorporation), s. 8 (corporate name), s. 115 (first directors); supplemented by O. Reg. 289/00 and Ontario Business Registry operational rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry, administered by the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the OBCA), filed electronically via the Ontario Business Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the OBCA; a private Ontario business corporation may be incorporated with nominal authorized share capital and shares issued for no less than CAD $1.00 each. No escrow account, capital deposit, or collateralized share subscription is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation adopt its Articles of Incorporation and commence business upon issuance of the certificate; FURTHER RESOLVED, that one thousand (1,000) common shares be issued to the founding subscriber at CAD $1.00 per share, and the Chief Executive Officer is authorized to issue share certificate number 1; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at the address stated in the Articles and records are maintained there; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the officers may open bank accounts, sign agreements and effect regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (ServiceOntario corporate name search portal; NUANS search system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS corporate name search to confirm the proposed name is distinguishable from existing Ontario and Federal corporate names. Reserve the approved name with the Ontario Business Registry for up to 90 days. Alternatively, adopt a numeric name (e.g., 1234567 Ontario Inc.) to expedite incorporation without a name search.
required_dossiers: Name search and reservation fee payment receipt (CAD $14)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as confusingly similar, prepare a revised name search and re-file the reservation; if the reservation is declined for administrative reasons, request an administrative review with the Assistant Registrar of Companies and resubmit corrected particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (online incorporation filing portal, ontario.ca/businessregistry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation questionnaire: select corporate name or numeric name, state the registered office address, list first directors, define authorized share structure and any restricted business activities, and certify the Articles of Incorporation. Electronically sign the Articles, pay the applicable CAD $300 filing fee, and receive an electronic acknowledgement of filing.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as first director for each director
Registered office and records address particulars
Payment confirmation for CAD $300 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query notice, respond through the Ontario Business Registry corrected filing channel with the required statutory declaration or amended schedules; if the filing is rejected on fee or signature grounds, re-authenticate the submission and re-file within 30 days of the defect notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Minute Book Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Director, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch; certificate retrieval via Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the electronic Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Director. Establish the corporate minute book, prepare By-law No. 1, issue the initial share certificate for the subscribed shares, and record the first directors' resolution and organizational resolutions. Order a certified copy of the certificate if required by banks or the CRA.
required_dossiers: By-law No. 1 approved by the first director
Share certificate stub and share register
Initial Notice of Registered Office and Directors if not included in the Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For typographical or minor errors appearing on the certificate, apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction under the OBCA; for substantive changes to share capital or name, file Articles of Amendment after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registration and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA using the 9-digit Business Number (BN) evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation. Activate the GST/HST account (mandatory once taxable worldwide revenue exceeds CAD $30,000), the payroll deductions program account for employee remuneration, and the import/export program account for resin and chemical raw material imports.
required_dossiers: Payroll and import/export program account registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is not activated or the program account is rejected, contact the CRA Business Window with the certificate of incorporation to verify identity and re-submit the registration; missing or updated information can be corrected through the CRA 'Change your business' service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning, Business Licence and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal zoning and licensing department; local fire department; Electrical Safety Authority (ESA); Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the casting premises are zoned for artisan light manufacturing and obtain a municipal business licence. Schedule a fire safety inspection under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), arrange an ESA electrical inspection for workshop equipment, and register with the WSIB as an employer if hiring workers. Retain all clearance certificates in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Zoning compliance letter or occupancy permit
ESA certificate of inspection for electrical installations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning refuses manufacturing use, apply to the local Committee of Adjustment for a minor variance or relocate to a permitted industrial unit; if fire deficiencies are identified, rectify the deficiencies and request re-inspection before commencing operations; disputed WSIB classification may be appealed to the Workplace Safety and Insurance Appeals Tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) – Consumer Product Safety Directorate; Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD) for workplace safety enforcement
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No federal industrial manufacturing licence is required for tabletop polyhedral dice casting. Product compliance is mandatory under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (S.C. 2010, c. 21) and the Toys Regulations (SOR/2011-17) where dice are marketed for children under 3 years. A general municipal business licence and occupancy permit are required for the casting premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – registration under the Environmental Activity and Sector Registry (EASR) or a site-specific Environmental Compliance Approval may be triggered only if volatile organic compound (VOC) usage exceeds 500 kg per year or if wastewater discharge thresholds are crossed; micro-scale hand resin casting normally qualifies for exemption from a full Environmental Impact Assessment, subject to EASR screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emissions (styrene, toluene, acetone) limited under O. Reg. 419/05 air dispersion standards; wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must comply with the local sewer use by-law (typically pH 6.0-9.0, no uncured liquid resin, no free-floating particulates); hazardous waste under O. Reg. 347 requires waste manifests and accumulation site registration where expired or uncured epoxy resin exceeds prescribed thresholds; empty catalyst and hardener containers must be classified for disposal according to the supplier SDS and O. Reg. 347.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), including storage limits for flammable uncured resins and hardeners; Electrical Safety Authority inspection certificate for workshop lighting and equipment circuits; building occupancy permit confirming structural load compliance for the casting premises; WHMIS 2015 worker training and Safety Data Sheet access; WSIB coverage clearance as an employer of record under the Workplace Safety and Insurance Act, 1997.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — official online portal: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account; Ontario corporate tax is administered by the CRA with the Ontario Ministry of Finance under the Canada–Ontario cooperative tax administration arrangement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Ontario business corporation, after federal (CBCA) or provincial (OBCA) incorporation and any required Ontario extra-provincial registration, the corporation must register with CRA by filing Form RC1 or using Business Registration Online (BRO). CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and activates separate program accounts for corporate income tax (RC) and GST/HST (RT); no separate national VAT ID exists. Required documentary support normally includes articles of incorporation, director identity details, Canadian registered-office address, and the expected date of first taxable activity. Registration should occur before the first reporting period; the GST/HST account must be active before invoicing export supplies at 0%, and the corporation should maintain its CRA My Business Account and authorized representative mandates for ongoing filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election for corporations. A resident corporation is automatically a separate taxpayer for federal and Ontario corporate income tax. Available statutory elections relevant to this structure include Income Tax Act s.85/88 rollover elections for corporate reorganizations, s.83(2) capital dividend election, s.216/217 elections for non-resident net-basis taxation, and Excise Tax Act s.156 closely related corporation election for GST/HST. Hybrid mismatch and interest-stripping rules operate automatically with limited elective scope.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax): 5% federal GST plus 8% Ontario provincial HST integrated as a single 13% HST administered by the CRA
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated export supplies, excluding financial services) in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; suppliers below the threshold may voluntarily register, which is normally advisable to claim input tax credits and support zero-rated exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Canada has no national real-time fiscal clearance regime, no mandatory e-invoice clearance network, and no digital stamping requirement. CRA requires registrants to file GST/HST returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or approved accounting software; e-invoice exchange remains voluntary, but all invoice and export substantiation records must be retained in a form acceptable to the CRA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the sale and export of tangible personal property (epoxy-resin polyhedral dice and accessories) if the property is exported by the supplier or by a common carrier, by mail/courier to an outside-Canada destination, or is shipped as part of a continuous journey to a destination outside Canada and proper evidence of export is retained. Services to non-residents may also be zero-rated when the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST and the service is not supplied to or for the benefit of a person present in Canada and is not in respect of Canadian real property or goods situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; the registrant should document the foreign destination, foreign counterparty, and payment flow.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Canadian Automated Export Declaration or current CBSA electronic export reporting) required for shipments valued above CAD 2,000 or controlled/regulated goods
Bill of Lading / airway waybill / postal customs declaration evidencing physical export from Canada
Commercial invoice and contract/sales order with ISIC 3240 and NAICS 339930 product description, export destination, and express 'zero-rated export supply' notation
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment confirmation proving receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident buyer
Export packing list and carrier tracking history to corroborate the transportation route
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period, or longer where misrepresentation or fraud is established. If an export zero-rating claim fails substantiation, the CRA will reassess the supply at 13%, disallow input tax credits/refunds, claw back paid refunds, and charge compounded daily arrears interest. Civil penalties may be assessed under Excise Tax Act s.280 for false statements, and intentional evasion can lead to criminal prosecution under s.327 with fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment; directors/owners may also become jointly and severally liable for unremitted HST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada (central monetary authority); no separate foreign exchange control administration; OSFI regulates banks, and FINTRAC, under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, oversees AML compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts. There are no statutory restrictions on profit remittances, dividend distributions, or repatriation of capital to non-residents, provided applicable Canadian withholding taxes (Part XIII tax on dividends and interest, Part XIV branch tax) are met, transfer pricing rules are complied with, and tax information reporting (Form T1135 for specified foreign assets) is current. Cross-border payments require no central bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export proceeds surrender requirement nor mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may maintain foreign-currency accounts and use export receipts directly for offshore procurement. Reporting obligations are limited to monthly sales tax/GST-HST returns, export declaration statistics via the CBSA, and residual foreign asset/tax disclosures; no repatriation deadline exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Cross-Border Clearing Package
Operational Account and International Settlement Account
Operational Account with US Dollar Receipt Capability
Operational Account and Liquidity Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium (viable as a supplemental settlement and currency-conversion rail, not as a primary treasury vehicle). Legal constraints: Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not authorized deposit-taking institutions in Canada and are not eligible for Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) protection. If an EMI collects payments from Canadian customers it must comply with Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act and obtain registration under applicable Canadian payment regulation. The EMI must also support FATCA/CRS reporting and sanctions screening. The Canadian entity should use EMIs for last-mile payouts and small-value crowdfunding settlements while concentrating the majority of liquidity in a CDIC-insured Schedule I bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC is permitted for a Canadian-incorporated entity where the authorized officers complete video ID verification and electronic signature. Banks may require physical branch attendance when the corporation has non-resident directors, complex multi-layer beneficial ownership, or identifiable PEP connections. For the stated low-risk tabletop gaming accessories company with resident directors, fully remote onboarding is generally available under OSFI-compliant digital identity protocols, subject to each bank's internal policy and FINTRAC obligations. Instruct all signatories to have original passports and proof-of-residence documentation ready if in-person verification is invoked.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume crowdfunding and pre-sale deposit concentration through Kickstarter/Stripe without a historical banking relationship, screened as unusual third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crowdfunding campaign contract and full data export with backer names, amounts and dates; processed Stripe settlement reports; refund policy and fulfilment plan; business plan and sales forecast; sample product invoices; board resolution on commercial funding; source-of-funds declarations from third-party processors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixed use of PayPal/Stripe in personal and business contexts with live gaming product sales, generating FX conversion surges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PayPal Business and Stripe Merchant ID statements; website domain and VAT/GST-HST registration; product catalogue and pricing; merchant-of-record agreements; AML/KYC questionnaires; customer dispute register; anti-money-laundering policy; UBO schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International procurement from Chinese and Indian epoxy resin and polyhedral-dice suppliers, viewed as sanctions exposure or trade-based money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full purchase contracts and commercial invoices; HS classification 3240/3399; packing lists and courier waybills; global supplier due-diligence records; certificate of origin where applicable; export/import permits; supplier bank reference and cancellation/refund policies; end-user/end-use attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity with low capital and no physical storefront, appearing shell-like in bank risk models.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Certificate of Incorporation and Articles; beneficial-ownership registry (update filed with Corporations Canada); registered-office address and utility bill; office/warehouse lease or coworking membership; GST/HST account confirmation; employer number if payroll expected; funding roadmap showing capitalization via share subscription and product revenues.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital injections must arrive via a recognized financial institution using SWIFT MT103 messaging. Each transfer should include the corporate name, Ontario company number, and the unrestricted reference 'CAPITAL INJECTION'. The receiving bank will require a board resolution authorizing the share issuance, executed subscription agreement, share certificate, and proof of funds from the shareholder's institution for source-of-wealth verification. Where a non-resident investor subscribes for equity, an Investment Canada Act review threshold may apply only when percentage of control reaches specified monetary bands; otherwise a notification to Statistics Canada under the Balance of Payments survey program is filed. Avoid routing through crypto-assets, unlicensed remitters, or same-day split wires, which trigger Reg R clearance and possible return of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational supplier payments are executed using SWIFT MT103 Corporate Payments via the corporate bank's treasury portal, with the beneficiary's IBAN/SWIFT address and full commercial-invoice matching mandated. For letters of credit, the Canadian bank issues a documentary Commercial LC under SWIFT MT700, typically irrevocable and confirmed by the exporter's bank, covering shipments of epoxy resins, molds, pigments, or finished dice; the instrument must include ICC UCP 600 terms and documentary requirements (invoice, packing list, bill of lading, quality inspection certificate). All outbound beneficiary countries are screened against Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists and OFAC screening. Payments are disbursed from a dual-approval environment with transaction limits set in the operating account agreement; FX conversion uses the bank's auto-hedge token to fix conversion for the date certain.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward (FXA) with Schedule I banks, primarily CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, for committed procurement payments and forecast export proceeds up to 12 months forward.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, MXN) where CAD is not deliverable; permitted only when the underlying trade invoice and payment schedule are separately documented.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CIRS) under ISDA/CSA documentation used to align foreign-currency liabilities from imports or export-finance loans with CAD cash flows, and to establish a permanent currency-swap hedge of net invested capital.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (15% federal Part I general rate + 11.5% Ontario general corporate rate); CCPC active business income eligible for the federal small business deduction: 12.2% combined (9% federal SBD rate + 3.2% Ontario small business rate on first C$500,000 of active business income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction: 9% federal rate on first C$500,000 of active business income for CCPCs (reduced at C$10M–C$15M taxable capital).
